theory.intro: Plotting $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$ against $\theta$ shows they are **periodic** — the graphs repeat. Sine and cosine are smooth waves between $-1$ and $1$; tangent has vertical asymptotes and repeats every $180^{\circ}$.
facts: $y=\sin\theta$ and $y=\cos\theta$ oscillate between $-1$ and $1$ and have period $360^{\circ}$.

$y=\sin\theta$ starts at $(0,0)$, peaks at $90^{\circ}$, is $0$ at $180^{\circ}$, troughs at $270^{\circ}$, and returns to $0$ at $360^{\circ}$.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$\theta$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-25, xmax=405, xtick={90,180,270,360},
  axis on top, xticklabel style={fill=white, inner sep=1.5pt},
  xmajorgrids, ymajorgrids, grid style={gray!25},
  samples=200, clip=true,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm,
  ymin=-1.45, ymax=1.45, ytick={-1,-0.5,0.5,1}]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:360] {sin(x)};
\node at (axis cs:290,1.1) {$y=\sin\theta$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

$y=\cos\theta$ starts at $(0,1)$, is $0$ at $90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$, troughs at $180^{\circ}$, and is $y=\sin\theta$ shifted $90^{\circ}$ to the left.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$\theta$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-25, xmax=405, xtick={90,180,270,360},
  axis on top, xticklabel style={fill=white, inner sep=1.5pt},
  xmajorgrids, ymajorgrids, grid style={gray!25},
  samples=200, clip=true,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm,
  ymin=-1.45, ymax=1.45, ytick={-1,-0.5,0.5,1}]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:360] {cos(x)};
\node at (axis cs:180,1.1) {$y=\cos\theta$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The curve starts at $(0,1)$ and falls to zero at $90^{\circ}$, so it is $y=\cos\theta$.

(b) One complete wave spans $360^{\circ}$. The period is $360^{\circ}$ and the maximum value is $1$.

(c) The lowest point is $(180,-1)$. The minimum value is $-1$, at $\theta=180^{\circ}$.

(d) The curve is above the horizontal axis for $0^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}<\theta<360^{\circ}$.

(e) At $50^{\circ}$ the curve is above the axis; at $160^{\circ}$ it is below. Therefore, $\cos50^{\circ}>\cos160^{\circ}$.

(f) Read every point where the curve crosses the horizontal axis, where $y=0$. The crossings are at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$.

The repeating increasing branches and vertical asymptotes identify $y=\tan\theta$.

Corresponding branches are $180^{\circ}$ apart, so its period is $180^{\circ}$.

The vertical asymptotes are at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $\theta=270^{\circ}$. Here $\cos\theta=0$, so $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ is undefined.

Tangent has neither a maximum nor a minimum; the branches continue beyond the plotted window.

Which trigonometric function does this graph show: $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$ or $\tan\theta$?
foundation.solution_text:

mastery.solution_text:
The horizontal line $y=-0.5$ meets the sine curve twice in each full cycle.
The interval $-720^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ spans three full cycles, and neither endpoint has sine value $-0.5$.
So there are $2\times3=6$ solutions.

mastery.question_text:
The equation $\sin\theta=0.5$ has a fixed number of solutions in each turn of the sine graph.
Using the period of $y=\sin\theta$, how many solutions does $\sin\theta=0.5$ have in $-360^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$?
mastery.solution_text:
In each $360^{\circ}$ cycle the line $y=0.5$ meets the sine curve twice (once rising, once falling).
The interval $-360^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ spans two full cycles.
So there are $2\times2=4$ solutions.

The two curves cross where their heights are equal.
From the graph this happens at $\theta=45^{\circ}$ and $\theta=225^{\circ}$.
